To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Gluconbacter kondonii cells efficiently catalyze the removal of acetaldehdye from the saliva after alcohol consumption and that the treated cells can be used as microcapsules to remove AA without the addition of cofactors.

Gluconbacter kondonii cells efficiently remove acetaldehyde from saliva after drinking without the supplemental addition cofactors, even in the case of excess ethanol, and that the cells retain their acetaldehyde decomposing activity after heat treatment.

a viable or non-viable Gluconobactor kondonii strain can be used for the catalytic decompostion of acetaldehyde from saliva without the supplemental addtion of cofactors, even in the presense of an excess of ethanole, and that this method can be used for reducing the risk for upper aerodigestiv tract cancer among aldehyde deshydrogenase 1 inactive heterozygous individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the catalytic removal and detoxification of AA in saliva by the use of a GK strain.
the development of an effective method for reducing the mutagenic risk of AA in saliva after drinking.
the catalytic decomposition of salivary AA by a GK strain and its application to the prevention of alcohol related UDA cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonviable GK cells are a promising agent for the catalytical removal of AA from saliva.
a GK strain is useful for the catalytic decomposing of AA in saliva after drinking.
a GK cell is a promising candidate for the catalytic decomposer of salivary AA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonviable GK cells could be used as a useful agent to remove AA from saliva after drinking.
the catalytic removal method using nonviable GK cells would be a useful strategy for reducing the risk for alcohol related UDAT cancers.
the catalytic removal method using the GK cells could be a promising strategy to reduce the risk of alcohol associated UDAT cancer in aldehyde dehydrogense 2 inactive heterzygotes.

the nonviable GK microcapsules could be used for the catalytic decomposing of salivary AA after drinking, thereby reducing the risk of cancer.
GK cells can be used as a catalyst for the removal of AA in the saliva to a concentration below its mutagenetic concentration after drinking.
